model.chat_prefix: Answer the question below the way a general-purpose AI assistant would, not as a coding agent: give a complete, well-structured answer the person can act on, using headings, lists or tables where they help. For advice, a plan or a proposal, give your recommendation first, then a concrete example detailed enough to follow, with steps, quantities or ranges, alternatives and how to adjust them as relevant. If personal details are missing, state your assumptions and who the answer suits. Follow any length the person asks for, and keep simple factual answers short. Apart from viewing the attachments listed below, do not read or write local files or run commands unless the question really needs it. Answer in the language of the question.
model.attach_intro_paths: Attached files ({n}). Their text content is included below. The original files are saved on this computer; open them read-only if you need images, charts, formulas or layout that the text does not capture.
model.attach_no_text_paths: (No text could be extracted. Open the original file to view it.)
model.attach_no_text: (No text could be extracted, e.g. an image.)
model.attach_trunc_paths: …(only the first {cap} characters are included; open the file for the rest)
model.peers_intro: For reference, here are the other models' answers to the previous question. Your own previous answer is in our conversation history; together they are all the answers from that round.
model.transcript_intro: Below is our conversation so far. Answer the new question at the end with it in mind.
model.judge_attach_intro: The question came with attachments. Their text is below for checking the answers.
model.title_prompt:
Write a title for a conversation that starts with the question below, capturing its core in at most 8 words. Output only the title, with no quotes, final period or explanation.

{q}

intro: You are a strict, fair reviewer. Below are several anonymous answers to the same question, labeled Answer A, Answer B, Answer C…, in random order.
Judge on content only. Do not guess or consider which model wrote each one. Do not use any tools or read or write files.
judge.earlier_intro: This is one round of a multi-turn conversation. Before this, the user asked, in order:
judge.earlier_note: (Each answerer can see its own earlier conversation.)
criteria: Scoring criteria (1 to 5 each, 5 is best):
- accuracy: are the facts correct, with no errors or fabrication
- completeness: does it cover the key aspects of the question
- clarity: is it well structured and easy to read
- usefulness: does it genuinely help the person who asked
- overall 1 to 5: your overall judgment, not a simple average
Also find where the answers agree and where they disagree:
- consensus: key conclusions all answers share, at most 5, one sentence each.

- conflicts: substantive disagreements between answers, at most 6. List only differences in content (facts, numbers, conclusions, advice, approach), not in wording, length or formatting. Use an empty array if there are none. Each has:
- topic: the point of disagreement, one sentence.
- kind: fact (facts or numbers conflict, so at least one is wrong), advice (different recommendations or approaches) or emphasis (different priorities or trade-offs).
- positions: what each answer says on this point, one sentence each; write "not mentioned" if it does not address it.
- verdict: which position is more credible and why; if you cannot tell, say how to check.
judge.format_intro: Output only one JSON object and no other text. Format:
judge.format_example: {"scores":{"A":{"accuracy":4,"completeness":4,"clarity":5,"usefulness":4,"overall":4,"comment":"one-sentence comment in English"}},"best":"A","reason":"one or two sentences in English on why it is best","consensus":["one sentence"],"conflicts":[{"topic":"one sentence","kind":"fact","positions":{"A":"one sentence","B":"one sentence"},"verdict":"one or two sentences"}]}
judge.format_note: Include every answer in scores and in each positions object. Refer to answers as "Answer A", "Answer B" and so on. If they are too close to call, set best to "tie".

explain: Explain {{concept}} in plain language: what it is, why it matters, a concrete example, and common misconceptions.
three-levels: Explain {{topic}} at three levels: an analogy a ten-year-old would get, a university-level explanation, then the details and debates experts care about.
concept-diff: How do {{concept A}} and {{concept B}} differ, and how are they related? Use a comparison table for definition, where each applies and a typical example, then point out where people most often confuse them.
learning-plan: I want to learn {{skill}} in {{time frame}}. My current level is {{current level}} and I can spend {{time per day}} a day. Give me a week-by-week plan: goals, concrete exercises, recommended resources, and how to check that I have really learned it.
quiz-me: Write 10 questions on {{topic}}, from easy to hard, mixing multiple choice and short answer. List only the questions first; after I answer, mark them and explain.
background: Walk me through the story of {{event or idea}}: the context, key people and turning points, the main schools of thought or positions, and its influence today. End with a few books worth reading.
polish:
Polish the text below. Keep the meaning and tone, and make it clearer, shorter and more natural. Give the revised version first, then list the main changes and why.

{{paste text}}
email:
Write an email to {{recipient}} to {{purpose}}. Tone: {{formal / friendly / brief}}. Keep it under 150 words and include a subject line. Key points:
{{key points}}
rewrite-audience:
Rewrite the content below for {{audience}}: drop jargon they don't need, add the background they do, and keep it to about {{length}} words.

{{paste content}}
outline: Outline an article about {{topic}} for {{readers}}. Give 3 title options, section headings with the points each section covers, and write the opening paragraph.
titles:
Suggest 10 headlines for the content below in three styles: straightforward, attention-grabbing and question-based. Say which one you recommend and why.

{{content summary}}
strict-editor:
Review the text below like a strict editor: point out logical gaps, weak evidence, wordiness and vague spots, ranked by importance, each with a suggested fix.

{{paste text}}
code-review:
Review the code below. List issues by severity (bugs, security, performance, readability), each with a suggested fix and example code:

{{paste code}}
explain-code:
Explain the code below section by section: what it does and why it is written this way. Point out hidden assumptions and edge cases where it could break.

{{paste code}}
unit-tests:
Write unit tests for the function below using {{test framework}}. Cover normal cases, edge cases and bad input, and say what each test checks.

{{paste code}}
refactor:
Refactor the code below without changing its behavior, aiming for better {{readability / performance / testability}}. Show the result and explain each change.

{{paste code}}
tech-choice: I'm building {{project}} and choosing between {{option A}}, {{option B}} and {{option C}}. Compare learning curve, performance, ecosystem, maintenance cost and fit with my team, then recommend one. Team: {{team details}}
regex: Write a regular expression that matches {{what to match}} but not {{what to exclude}}. Explain it piece by piece and give 5 strings that should match and 5 that should not.
system-design: Design {{system}} for {{users / requests}}. Describe the architecture, core components, data model and key trade-offs, and what would change at ten times the scale.
compare-options: Compare {{option A}} and {{option B}}: where each fits, pros and cons, cost and risk. End with your recommendation and why.
decide: I'm considering {{decision}}. My situation: {{background}}. List the reasons for and against, the key uncertainties, the worst case and how I'd handle it. Then give your advice and what would make you change your mind.
premortem: Imagine that a year from now {{plan}} has failed completely. List the 8 most likely reasons, ranked by likelihood and impact, each with something I can do now to prevent it.
devils-advocate: My view: {{your view}}. Argue the other side as strongly as you can, with evidence, then point out the weakest part of my view.
prioritize:
Here are my tasks. Rank them by importance and urgency with reasons, and suggest which to postpone, delegate or drop:

{{task list}}
meeting-notes:
Turn the notes below into meeting minutes: conclusions, decisions, action items (owner and due date) and open questions.

{{paste notes}}
weekly-report:
Write a weekly report from the notes below: done this week, key numbers, problems, plan for next week. Keep it brief; the reader is {{reader}}.

{{work notes}}
exec-summary:
Condense the content below into a one-page brief for leadership: a one-sentence conclusion, three key points, and the decision or support you need from them.

{{content}}
project-plan: Draft a plan for {{project}}: goals and success criteria, milestones and timeline, resources needed, and the main risks with mitigations. The deadline is {{date}}.
feedback: Help me write feedback for {{person}}. Situation: {{situation}}. Be specific and focus on the work, not the person: start with what went well, then what to improve and how.
interview-prep: I'm interviewing for {{role}} at {{company}}. List the 10 most likely questions (half technical, half behavioral), with how to approach each and key points, plus 3 questions I can ask the interviewer.
research-state: Summarize the state of research on {{topic}}: main schools and leading figures, key studies and findings, and open or disputed questions. Separate established consensus from single-study findings, and suggest further reading.
market: Analyze {{market or industry}}: size and growth, main players and their strengths, customer needs, trends and risks. Flag which numbers need checking.
competitors: Compare {{product A}}, {{product B}} and {{product C}}: positioning, core features, pricing, pros and cons, and who each suits. Use a table and end with a recommendation.
summarize-article:
Summarize the article below in three sentences, list its main arguments and evidence, then judge whether the reasoning holds up and which opposing views it leaves out.

{{paste article}}
fact-check:
Fact-check the text below. Mark each claim or number as correct, wrong or unverifiable, and explain why:

{{paste text}}
credibility: I came across this claim: "{{claim}}". Assess how credible it is: likely sources, evidence for and against, common distorted versions, and how I can check it myself.
check-math:
Check the calculation and reasoning below: redo it step by step, point out any errors, and give the correct result.

{{paste content}}
compare-answers: Compare the models' answers from the last round: where they agree, where they contradict each other, and whose reasoning is stronger. Then combine them into the best answer.
find-gaps: Did the last answers miss any important cases, risks or counterexamples? Add them and explain how they change the conclusion.
more-concrete: Make the answer above more concrete: steps I can follow directly, specific numbers, and one complete worked example.
summarize-attachments: Summarize the attachments: give the conclusion in three sentences, then the key figures and any decisions I need to make.
doc-qa: Answer using only the attachments: {{question}}. Quote the text that supports your answer; if the attachments don't say, tell me instead of guessing.
extract-table: Extract {{information to extract}} from the attachments into a table, noting where each item appears (page or section).
analyze-sheet: Analyze the spreadsheet in the attachments: give an overview, find trends and outliers, list the 3 most important findings, and suggest what to analyze next.
contract: Read the contract in the attachments and list: each party's main obligations, payment and deadlines, liability for breach, termination terms, and clauses that are unfavorable to me or need attention. (This is not a substitute for legal advice.)
translate:
Translate the text below into {{target language}}, keeping the meaning and tone and using terms consistently. Where there are several possible renderings or cultural differences, add a short note after the translation.

{{paste text}}
ja-business-email:
Write a polite Japanese business email (with appropriate keigo) that says the following, with an English version alongside:

{{what to say}}
travel: Plan a {{number of days}}-day trip to {{destination}}. Travelers: {{who is going}}. Budget: {{budget}}. Preferences: {{preferences}}. Give a day-by-day plan, how to get around, where to stay, and things to watch out for.
buying-advice: I want to buy {{product type}} for {{main use}}, budget {{budget}}. Explain the specs that matter most, compare a few models, and tell me which you'd pick.
gift: Suggest gifts for {{person}} for {{occasion}}, budget {{budget}}; they like {{interests}}. Give 8 ideas with reasons, split into safe choices and more original ones.
improve-prompt:
Improve the prompt below so the AI's answer is more accurate and closer to what I need. Point out its problems first, then give the rewritten version:

{{original prompt}}
system-prompt: Write a system prompt for an AI assistant used for {{purpose}}: its role, target users, answer style, rules it must follow and things it must not do, plus two example conversations.
